A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImpForge and CrossGuard research. All 14 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated sections and renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety and utility evaluations, ImpForge attack-generation results, training-data ablations and a PPO comparison, including Tables 1–2 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds latency and memory measurements for three guard models in Appendix B.2 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The two-stage ImpForge pipeline, three reward functions, PPO optimization and LoRA-based CrossGuard binary classifier are retained. Condensed architecture descriptions and newly specified ablation implementations do not establish changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain the same, including JailBreakV, MM-SafetyBench, SIUO, FigStep, VLGuard and MMBench. Appendix C.1 newly documents subsets and sample counts within existing coverage; the computational-cost study introduces no new dataset or input scenario.

E2.justification: The main comparison methods and the in-context learning and LoRA fine-tuning alternatives are retained. The new computational-cost comparison reuses LlavaGuard and Llama-Guard3-Vision, both already evaluated in v1, without changing comparator membership in the existing experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a protocol measuring latency in seconds per item and memory in GB under a shared NVIDIA A40 configuration. Appendix C's sampling and ASR-scoring details describe existing evaluations; the PDFs do not establish that those evaluations changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an analysis of computational cost and the efficiency–security trade-off in Appendix B.2. The training-data ablation remains unchanged, and the existing PPO comparison moves from Appendix C.2/Figure 8 to Section 5.6/Figure 5. The expanded overfitting discussion introduces no additional robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or measurement uncertainty. The new latency and memory results also lack uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports latency/memory of 33.33 s/item and 33.68 GB for LlavaGuard, 0.63 and 21.32 for Llama-Guard3-Vision, and 0.24 and 14.14 for CrossGuard. Its JailBreakV ASRs repeat Table 1. Existing benchmark scores, attack-generation results, ablation plots and qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: The attack formulation, reward definitions, optimization objectives and binary classification loss in Equations 1–6 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds proofs or theoretical guarantees; the new ASR-scoring documentation concerns experimental implementation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: automated generation of implicit multimodal attacks and a safeguard balancing security and utility against explicit and implicit threats. Rewriting and additional efficiency evidence do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now interprets existing OOD results as evidence against synthetic-template memorization and for learned safety boundaries. The limitations discussion replaces the template/category-bias emphasis with pretrained reward-model bias and a claimed mitigation through relative judgments. Appendix B.2 adds an interpretation of deployment efficiency.

D1.justification: New Appendix C substantially expands reproducibility information: dataset subsets and sample counts, Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct ablation implementations, three SIUO demonstrations, and separate ASR-scoring procedures for commercial models, offline models and guardrails. Appendix B.2 specifies A40 hardware. These are newly disclosed details, not demonstrated revisions to existing experiments; the code link already existed in v1.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion moves from Appendix A to Section 2 while retaining its research coverage and positioning. Reference changes update author, title and publication metadata for the same discussed methods and resources, without a substantive expansion of the literature argument.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative by promoting related work and the PPO ablation into the main text and restructuring the appendices. It also rewrites the experimental setup, several analysis passages, conclusion and limitations, beyond simple renumbering or insertion of new results.

P2.justification: v2 adds computational-cost Table 3 and refusal-template Figure 9. Existing figures are retained, with the PPO plot relocated and renumbered from Figure 8 to Figure 5. Captions, figure placement and some table styling change, but the established visualizations are not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: Appendix C makes previously underspecified evaluations easier to audit and reproduce, while Table 3 provides measured support for computational practicality. These are useful, limited gains. The core validation remains unchanged, and the stronger anti-overfitting interpretation rests on existing OOD results rather than a direct memorization test. Earlier inconsistencies between Table 1 and its accompanying prose also remain.
